name: Social Insurance (Bảo hiểm xã hội)

references.title: Law 41/2024 arts.31(1)(b), 37(2): use actual qualifying stoppage salary; temporarily suspend compulsory SI during detention/disciplinary suspension, restore arrears when full wages are back-paid. A dated insurance_review supplies an exact monthly base/status; mixed and split months are not guessed.
Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 (Luật Bảo hiểm xã hội)
references.quote: Art.33–34: 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,340,000, ceiling 46,800,000). Employer 17.5% = 3% sickness and maternity + 14% retirement and survivorship + 0.5% occupational accident and disease; 17.3% where the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate applies. Above the ceiling the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate. Art.31(1)(đ): tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,340,000 đ). Art.33(5): an unpaid month of 14 or more working days is waived for the listed categories (not part-time employees, art.2(1)(l)), and may be continued by agreement at the most recent contribution base (arts.33(5), 34(3)); art.33(6): SI is due in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Art.53(8): birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave are exempt without the 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases only from 14 working days in the month. Art.2(1)(a): fixed-term contract covered only “từ đủ 01 tháng trở lên”. Art.2(7)(b): a domestic worker is not a compulsory participant. Art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age (measured at the contract’s signing) is excluded; also excluded: foreign employee on a contract under 12 months, intra-company transferee, treaty-exempt. Part-time pay below 2,340,000 is outside compulsory SI and UI.

references.title: Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP (Nghị định 158/2025/NĐ-CP)
references.quote: Insurance salary = the monthly job or title wage, plus the wage allowances and the other supplements of a stated amount agreed in the contract and paid regularly and stably each pay period, excluding items that depend on or vary with productivity, work history or performance (fixed allowance rows count; a row marked not fixed stays outside). A part-time employee’s base is the pay of the month (art.7(2)). Occupational-accident contributions stay on the compulsory SI salary (art.43(2)).

name: Đoàn phí công đoàn (union membership dues)

references.title: Law on Trade Unions 50/2024/QH15 (Luật Công đoàn)
references.quote: Union members in an enterprise outside the State sector pay dues; paid to the union, never by a non-member.

references.title: Decision 61/QĐ-TLĐ of the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour
references.quote: In force from 1 July 2025. A member in an enterprise outside the State sector pays dues of 0.5% of the salary the compulsory social insurance is based on, capped at 10% of the base salary (mức lương cơ sở) — at most 234,000 (10% of 2,340,000). Art.1 waives dues only for a member on SI benefit for a month or more, or without work, income or pay for a month or more — not for the 14 unpaid working days that end the month’s SI contribution (Law 41/2024 art.33(5)); such a member still pays 0.5% of the insurance salary. A member outside compulsory SI pays a set sum of at least 0.5% of the base salary, which the union sets. In a State-owned enterprise the dues are 0.5% of the take-home salary after SI, HI, UI and PIT, same cap. Owner rule 2026-11-04: this version computes State-sector and other members on the compulsory-SI wage base (actual ordinary pay plus fixed allowances), capped at 10% of the base salary; the bonus-inclusive GROSS checkpoint is not a dues base. Caveat (owner rule 2026-09-28, law silent on a part month): the waiver applies to a pay month in which every scheduled working day is wholly unpaid; maternity-benefit months stay waived as SI’s own exemption; a month with SI nil counts as a benefit month only for a birth, adoption, surrogate-birth or commissioning-mother maternity spell, not a paternity spell (at most 14 working days, art.53(2)) or a short maternity event (miscarriage, check-up, contraception).
